question.text: A bull call spread on NIFTY: buy 25000 call @ Rs. 120, sell 25200 call @ Rs. 60. Maximum profit per unit:

explanation.text: The Logic: A bull call spread is built by buying a lower-strike call and selling a higher-strike call of the same expiry. Maximum profit per unit = (Higher strike – Lower strike) – Net premium paid. Net premium paid here = Rs. 120 – Rs. 60 = Rs. 60. Spread width = 25200 – 25000 = 200. Maximum profit = 200 – 60 = Rs. 140 per unit, achieved when the underlying closes at or above the higher strike at expiry. The Trap: 'Rs. 60' is the net premium paid (which equals the maximum loss, not the maximum profit). 'Rs. 120' is just the long-call premium. 'Rs. 200' is the gross spread width without netting the cost of the spread. Note: Bull call spreads, spread width, net premium and maximum-profit payoff calculations are not covered in the cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook pages checked, which define options and option writer/buyer obligations only. The framing above is presented as general options-strategy knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
